facts.raw_span: A man in his 70s presented with swelling of the manubrium
12 years after resection of a large left substernal thyroid lobe through a midline sternotomy approach
The swelling was slightly tender and had increased in size markedly over the month prior to presentation
Swelling noted over the manubrium, which was slightly tender
lytic lesion replacing the manubrium measuring 2.7 × 4.4 × 5.8 cm
residual right goiter
The posterior aspect is in close proximity to the brachiocephalic artery and the left innominate vein
Revealed follicular thyroid cells in the goiter and the manubrial lesion
Hematoxylin-eosin stained specimens showing thyroid follicles infiltrating adjacent to bone trabeculae
previous substernal left hemithyroidectomy for benign goiter 12 years ago

concepts.why: The patient has a history of thyroid surgery and now presents with a lytic lesion in the manubrium, which contains thyroid follicles, suggesting metastasis.
The patient has a history of goiter and now presents with residual goiter, suggesting incomplete removal or recurrence.
The patient has a history of thyroid surgery and now presents with a lesion at the surgical site, suggesting recurrence.
The patient presents with a lytic lesion in the manubrium, which is a characteristic feature of certain bone lesions.
The patient presents with a lesion in close proximity to the brachiocephalic artery and left innominate vein, suggesting potential vascular involvement.
The patient presents with tender swelling over the manubrium, which is a characteristic feature of inflammatory conditions.
The patient presents with thyroid follicles infiltrating adjacent to bone trabeculae, which is a characteristic feature of follicular thyroid carcinoma.
The patient presents with tender swelling over the manubrium, which could be a sign of postoperative infection.

rationales.F01: Swelling over the manubrium could be due to various causes, but the presence of follicular thyroid cells suggests a possible connection to thyroid conditions.
rationales.F02: Previous thyroid surgery increases the likelihood of thyroid-related conditions, including metastasis or recurrence.
rationales.F05: A lytic lesion in the manubrium with follicular thyroid cells is highly suggestive of thyroid metastasis to bone.
rationales.F06: Residual goiter is a possible cause of the swelling, and the presence of follicular thyroid cells supports this diagnosis.
rationales.F08: Follicular thyroid cells in the goiter and manubrial lesion strongly suggest a thyroid-related condition, such as metastasis or recurrence.
rationales.F09: Thyroid follicles infiltrating adjacent to bone trabeculae is a characteristic feature of thyroid metastasis to bone.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of a lytic lesion in the manubrium with follicular thyroid cells and the patient's history of thyroid lobe resection support the diagnosis of thyroid metastasis to bone, which is further strengthened by the pathological examination showing thyroid follicles infiltrating adjacent to bone trabeculae.
